title: Rivers
source: Courses from OpenStreetMap (relations and named ways, by id); tributaries and distributaries after the notes' Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna, Kaveri and Brahmaputra maps

places.name: Godavari

source.name: Trambakeshwar
source.significance: Where the Godavari rises, in the Brahmagiri hills of the Western Ghats near Nashik

places.significance: The longest river of the peninsula — the 'Dakshin Ganga' — rising in the Western Ghats near Nashik and crossing the whole Deccan to the Bay of Bengal
notes: Rises at Trambakeshwar in the Brahmagiri hills, near Nashik (Maharashtra)
Flows through Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; its basin also drains Chhattisgarh and Odisha
Splits below Rajahmundry, at Dowleswaram, into the Gautami and the Vasishta, which build its delta

places.name: Gautami Godavari
places.significance: The eastern of the two great delta branches from Dowleswaram, reaching the sea near Yanam

places.name: Vasishta Godavari
places.significance: The western delta branch from Dowleswaram, reaching the sea at Antarvedi

places.name: Pravara
places.significance: Right-bank tributary from the Western Ghats near Ratangad, dammed at Bhandardara, meeting its parent near Newasa

places.name: Mula
places.significance: Rises in the Harishchandragad hills and is dammed at Rahuri before joining the Pravara near Newasa
notes: A tributary of the Pravara, not of the Godavari directly

places.name: Manjara
places.significance: Right-bank tributary from the Balaghat range in Beed, past Latur and the Nizam Sagar dam, joining near Kandakurthi in Telangana

places.name: Maner
places.significance: Telangana tributary through Karimnagar, dammed above the city, joining near Manthani

places.name: Kinnarsani
places.significance: Comes down from the forests of Bhadradri Kothagudem, whose wildlife sanctuary carries its name, to join near Bhadrachalam

places.name: Purna
places.significance: Left-bank tributary rising in the Ajanta range and draining Marathwada through Jalna and Parbhani — not the Tapi's river of the same name
notes: Rises in the Ajanta range

places.name: Dudhna
places.significance: Rises in the Ajanta hills near Aurangabad and joins the Purna in Parbhani district
notes: A tributary of the Purna

places.name: Penganga
places.significance: Rises in the Ajanta range in Buldhana and forms much of the Maharashtra–Telangana border before joining the Wardha
notes: A tributary of the Wardha

places.name: Wardha
places.significance: Rises in the Satpura range near Multai in Betul, gathers the Penganga, and with the Wainganga forms the Pranhita

places.name: Wainganga
places.significance: Rises in the Mahadeo Hills of Seoni and flows south past Bhandara and Gadchiroli; with the Wardha it forms the Pranhita

places.name: Kanhan
places.significance: Flows past the north of Nagpur, gathering the Pench, into the Wainganga
notes: Drawn only to carry the Pench to the Wainganga; never asked

places.name: Pench
places.significance: Rises in the Mahadeo Hills of Chhindwara and runs through the Seoni forests of the Jungle Book to join the Kanhan above Nagpur
notes: A tributary of the Kanhan, which carries it to the Wainganga

places.name: Pranhita
places.significance: The Wardha and the Wainganga combined — the largest tributary of all, meeting its parent at Kaleshwaram on the Maharashtra–Telangana border

places.name: Narangi
places.significance: A Bastar stream from the Kondagaon plateau, joining the Indravati
notes: A tributary of the Indravati

places.name: Indravati
places.significance: Rises in Odisha's Kalahandi and crosses Bastar over the Chitrakote Falls — 'India's Niagara' — to join where Maharashtra, Telangana and Chhattisgarh meet

places.name: Sabari
places.significance: Known in Odisha as the Kolab, it forms the Chhattisgarh–Odisha border and joins near Kunavaram above the Papi Hills gorge

places.name: Sileru
places.significance: Runs along the Andhra–Odisha border, its falls and dams harnessed for hydel power, to join the Sabari at Motu
notes: A tributary of the Sabari

places.name: Mahanadi

source.name: Sihawa
source.significance: Where the Mahanadi rises, in the hills of Chhattisgarh's Dhamtari district

places.significance: Rises near Sihawa in Chhattisgarh's Dhamtari district and is held back at Hirakud — one of the world's longest earthen dams — before its delta at Cuttack
notes: Rises near Sihawa (Dhamtari district, Chhattisgarh)
Flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha to the Bay of Bengal

places.name: Seonath
places.significance: The longest tributary, rising in Rajnandgaon and passing Durg to join at Shivrinarayan

places.name: Hasdo
places.significance: Flows south through the Korba coalfield, dammed at Bango, to join near Shivrinarayan

places.name: Mand
places.significance: Left-bank tributary from the Raigarh hills, joining near Chandrapur in Janjgir-Champa

places.name: Ib
places.significance: Rises in Jashpur's hills and empties into the reservoir behind Hirakud dam; its valley holds one of Odisha's main coalfields

places.name: Jonk
places.significance: Right-bank tributary from the Odisha border hills, flowing north through Mahasamund to join at Shivrinarayan

places.name: Ong
places.significance: Right-bank tributary through Bargarh district, joining above Sonepur

places.name: Tel
places.significance: The largest right-bank tributary, draining Kalahandi and Nabarangpur to join at Sonepur, Odisha's temple town

places.name: Kathajodi
places.significance: Branches off at Naraj above Cuttack and carries much of the delta's water past the city's south side

places.name: Devi
places.significance: A delta branch reaching the Bay of Bengal near Astaranga, where Olive Ridley turtles come ashore to nest
notes: Leaves the Kathajodi below Cuttack — a distributary, carrying water away from the main river to the sea

places.name: Krishna

source.name: Mahabaleshwar
source.significance: Where the Krishna rises, a hill station high in the Western Ghats of Satara district

places.significance: The peninsula's second-longest river, crossing the Deccan from the Western Ghats to the Bay of Bengal, held back at Almatti, Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar
notes: Rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats (Satara, Maharashtra)
Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal

places.name: Koyna
places.significance: Rises at Mahabaleshwar and powers Maharashtra's largest hydroelectric project before joining at Karad's Preeti Sangam

places.name: Varna
places.significance: Dammed at Chandoli in the Sahyadri, it runs along the Sangli–Kolhapur border to join at Haripur near Sangli

places.name: Panchganga
places.significance: Five streams meeting at Prayag Chikhali give Kolhapur its river, which joins at Narsobawadi, a Dattatreya pilgrimage town

places.name: Dudhganga
places.significance: Dammed at Kalammawadi in Kolhapur's hills, it crosses into Karnataka's Belagavi district to join

places.name: Ghatprabha
places.significance: Plunges over the Gokak Falls — the 'Niagara of Karnataka' — and is dammed at Hidkal before joining in Bagalkot

places.name: Malprabha
places.significance: Rises near Kanakumbi in the Western Ghats, is dammed at Navilutheertha, and joins at Kudalasangama, where Basavanna rests

places.name: Bhima
places.significance: Rises at a Jyotirlinga shrine in the Sahyadri above Pune, flows past the pilgrim town of Pandharpur, and joins near Raichur

places.name: Nira
places.significance: Rises in the Sahyadri near Bhor and divides Pune district from Satara before joining at Narsinghpur

places.name: Man
places.significance: Drains the drought-prone Mandesh of eastern Satara and Sangli to join near Pandharpur

places.name: Sina
places.significance: Rises near Ahmednagar and flows south-east through Solapur district to join at Kudal

places.name: Tungabhadra
places.significance: The Tunga and the Bhadra combined from Koodli, past Hampi and the Hosapete dam, to join near Alampur
notes: Drawn only to carry the Tunga and the Bhadra to the Krishna; never asked

places.name: Tunga
places.significance: Rises at Gangamoola in the Kudremukh hills and flows past Sringeri and Shivamogga to meet its twin at Koodli

places.name: Bhadra
places.significance: Rises at Gangamoola beside its twin, is dammed at Lakkavalli, and meets it at Koodli to form the river that carries both to the Krishna

places.name: Musi
places.significance: Hyderabad's river, on whose banks the city was founded, dammed at Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar above it, joining at Wazirabad

places.name: Munneru
places.significance: Comes down from the hills of Mahabubabad past Khammam to join above Vijayawada

places.name: Kaveri

source.name: Talakaveri
source.significance: Where the Kaveri rises, a sacred spring high in the hills of Kodagu on the Western Ghats

places.significance: The south's most disputed river, shared by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu: dammed at Krishnaraja Sagar and Mettur, falling at Shivanasamudra and Hogenakkal, and spreading into the Thanjavur delta
notes: Rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu (Karnataka)
Flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu to the Bay of Bengal

places.name: Hemavati
places.significance: Rises at Ballalarayanadurga in the Western Ghats of Chikkamagaluru, is dammed at Gorur, and joins near Krishnarajapete above the great reservoir

places.name: Shimsha
places.significance: Rises in Tumakuru's Devarayanadurga hills, flows past Maddur, and drops through a hydel cascade beside Shivanasamudra to join

places.name: Arkavati
places.significance: Bengaluru's old water supply, dammed at Hesaraghatta and Thippagondanahalli, joining at Sangama near Mekedatu

places.name: Lakshmantirtha
places.significance: Tumbles over the Iruppu Falls in southern Kodagu and joins at the Krishnaraja Sagar reservoir

places.name: Kabini
places.significance: Rises in Kerala's Wayanad and is dammed at Beechanahalli between the Nagarhole and Bandipur forests, joining at Tirumakudalu Narasipura

places.name: Suvarnavati
places.significance: Chamarajanagar district's river, flowing north past Yelandur to join near Kollegal

places.name: Bhavani
places.significance: Rises in the Nilgiris beside Kerala's Silent Valley, is held back by one of Asia's largest earthen dams, and joins at Kooduthurai in Erode

places.name: Noyyal
places.significance: Coimbatore's river, and Tiruppur's — dyed by the knitwear town's factories — joining near Kodumudi

places.name: Amaravati
places.significance: Rises in the Anaimalai hills, flows past Dharapuram, and joins at Karur

places.name: Thirumanimuthar
places.significance: Rises in Salem's Shevaroy hills and drains the city before joining near Paramathi Velur in Namakkal

places.name: Brahmaputra

source.name: Chemayungdung Glacier
source.significance: Where the Brahmaputra rises, in the Kailash range of Tibet south-east of Lake Mansarovar

places.significance: Crosses the roof of the world, bends round Namcha Barwa through the deepest gorge on Earth, and floods Assam's plain every monsoon before meeting the Padma (Ganga) in Bangladesh
notes: 1. **Tibet** → River: Yarlung Tsangpo, Origin: Chemayungdung Glacier
2. **Arunachal Pradesh** → Associated rivers: Dihang/Dibang, Pass: Yongyab Pass, Mountain: Namcha Barwa
3. **Assam** → Called the Sorrow of Assam, Island: Majuli
4. **Bangladesh** → Known as the **Jamuna**, which further becomes the **Meghna**, Delta: Sundarban delta

places.name: Subansiri
places.significance: Its largest tributary, rising in Tibet and cutting through Arunachal to join beside Majuli; dammed at Gerukamukh for India's biggest hydro project

places.name: Kameng
places.significance: Rises below Gori Chen on the Tawang border and runs past the Pakke tiger reserve, taking another name in Assam to join near Tezpur

places.name: Manas
places.significance: Comes down from Bhutan through a World Heritage tiger reserve on the border to join at Jogighopa

places.name: Gangadhar
places.significance: The Sankosh and the Raidak combined, from the Assam–West Bengal border into Bangladesh to meet the main stream
notes: Drawn only to carry the Sankosh and the Raidak to the Brahmaputra; never asked

places.name: Sankosh
places.significance: Rises in northern Bhutan, flows past Punakha's dzong, and forms the Assam–West Bengal border before joining near Bangladesh

places.name: Raidak
places.significance: Flows past Bhutan's capital, Thimphu, and the Chukha hydro project before crossing Alipurduar into Bangladesh

places.name: Jaldhaka
places.significance: Rises in the lakes of eastern Sikkim and crosses the Dooars, harnessed at Jhalong, on its way into Bangladesh

places.name: Teesta

source.name: Tso Lhamo Lake
source.significance: Where the Teesta rises, among the ice and high lakes of north Sikkim near the Tibet border

places.significance: Sikkim's lifeline, carving the state from north to south before crossing the Siliguri plain into Bangladesh, where sharing its water is a long dispute
notes: Rises at Zemu Glacier / Tso Lhamo Lake in north Sikkim

places.name: Rangit
places.significance: Sikkim's western river, from the glaciers below Kanchenjunga, meeting its parent at Melli below Darjeeling

places.name: Dibang
places.significance: Comes down from the Mishmi Hills of Arunachal, where India's tallest dam is being built, to meet its neighbour near Sadiya just above the main stream

places.name: Lohit
places.significance: The 'river of blood', named for the red earth it carries, entering India from Tibet at Kibithu and passing the pilgrim pool of Parshuram Kund
notes: Known as the river of blood (the red river)

places.name: Burhi Dihing
places.significance: Rises in the Patkai hills and runs past Digboi's century-old oilfield and the rainforest at Jeypore

places.name: Dhansiri
places.significance: Rises in Nagaland's hills and flows past Dimapur and Golaghat to join

places.name: Kopili
places.significance: Rises in Meghalaya's Jaintia hills, is harnessed at Umrangso for hydel power, and joins in Morigaon district

places.name: Majuli
places.significance: The world's largest river island, home to Assam's Vaishnavite satras, and shrinking with every monsoon flood
notes: In the Brahmaputra in Assam, between the main stream and the Subansiri

places.name: Namcha Barwa
places.significance: The 7,782m summit in Tibet round which the main stream makes its great bend south into India, through the deepest gorge on Earth

groups.name: Kaveri — left-bank tributaries
groups.mnemonic: C̶ H S A T — CSAT with the C struck out for an H: Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavati, Thirumanimuthar

groups.name: Kaveri — right-bank tributaries (L K S)
groups.mnemonic: L K S — Laksham ji Tirth se Kab aaye? Swarn hiran leke aaye: Lakshmantirtha, Kabini, Suvarnavati
